title: Verbal Aspect and Preverbs in Economic Restructuring

sections.title: Aspectual Transformations: át-, le-, fel-, meg-
sections.content: Hungarian captures systemic restructuring through productive prefix combinations. 'Átalakul' ('transforms / converts') marks structural metamorphosis from one paradigm to another: 'A nehézipar a szolgáltatások felé alakul át' ('Heavy industry transforms toward services'). 'Leépít' / 'leépül' ('downsizes / scales down / decays') captures the deliberate reduction of redundant capacity or workforces. 'Felzárkózik' ('catches up / converges') marks closing a competitive gap, while 'megszilárdul' ('stabilizes / consolidates') signals achieving equilibrium.

sections.title: Resultative Economics: modernizál vs. korszerűsít
sections.content: Institutional terminology pairs these preverbal verbs with abstract nouns of adaptation: 'szerkezeti átalakulás' ('structural transformation'), 'korszerűsítés' ('modernization / retrofitting'), 'versenyképesség' ('competitiveness'), and 'alkalmazkodóképesség' ('adaptive capacity / resilience'). Precision in matching preverbs to economic phases ensures authentic upper-intermediate register.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Distinguish transitive 'leépít valamit' (the management downsizes a plant) from reflexive/passive 'leépül' (capacities degrade or downsize on their own).
